The decisive test is not whether prose looks cleaner. It is whether readers: make better decisions, preserve fewer false certainties, escalate sooner, fund better proposals, forgive failures appropriately, and reconstruct decisions later.

Every technique in the set is currently evaluated by proxies (readability scores, tell counts, expert judgment) rather than decision outcomes. This is the missing evidence base and it is missing for all techniques, not just some.

Overall pattern: Institutional adoption and practitioner consensus dominate. Direct experimental evidence linking specific techniques to organizational outcomes (better decisions, higher trust, fewer repeated incidents, less aggregation decay) is sparse.
